title: Performance and caching
summary: Measuring before optimising, memory leaks and the garbage collector, caching strategies, and protecting services with rate limits.

sections.title: Measure first
sections.body:
Start with numbers: request latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), throughput, event loop delay, CPU and heap. Profile with `node --cpu-prof` or the inspector (`--inspect`) and read the flame graph for the widest frames. `performance.now()` and `perf_hooks` give precise timings in code.

Typical wins are boring: add a database index, remove an N+1 query, stream instead of buffering, cache a hot read, and avoid `JSON.stringify` on huge objects.

sections.title: Memory and leaks
sections.body:
V8 frees objects that are no longer reachable. A leak is memory that stays reachable by mistake: a module-level `Map` used as a cache with no limit, listeners never removed, closures holding big objects, timers never cleared. Watch `heapUsed` over time and compare heap snapshots to find what keeps growing.

Every cache needs a bound: a maximum size with an eviction policy such as LRU, a TTL, or both. `WeakMap` and `WeakRef` help when the key's lifetime should decide the entry's lifetime.

sections.title: Caching
sections.body:
Cache where it pays: in-process (fast, per instance, lost on restart), shared (Redis), or HTTP (`Cache-Control`, `ETag` and a CDN). With **cache-aside**, read from the cache, fall back to the source and store the result.

Two traps: **stampedes**, where many requests miss at once and all hit the database (fix: share one in-flight promise per key), and **stale data** (fix: TTLs plus invalidation on writes).

sections.title: Rate limiting
sections.body: Protect your service and its dependencies with limits per client: a **token bucket** refills at a fixed rate and allows short bursts up to its capacity; a **sliding window** counts requests in the last N seconds. Return `429` with `Retry-After`. In a multi-instance deployment the counters must live in a shared store.

pitfalls: Optimising without a profile or a benchmark.
An unbounded in-memory cache that grows until the process is killed.
Caching without a plan for invalidation.
Per-instance rate limits behind a load balancer.

gotchas.question: What is a cache stampede and how do you prevent it?
gotchas.answer: When a popular key expires, many concurrent requests miss and all recompute it, overloading the source. Prevent it by sharing one in-flight promise per key, refreshing slightly before expiry, or adding jitter to TTLs.

gotchas.question: Why does a Map keep growing even after requests finish?
gotchas.answer: Because the Map is reachable from module scope, so everything stored in it stays reachable. The garbage collector only frees unreachable objects. Bound it or delete entries explicitly.

gotchas.question: How do you implement an LRU cache in JavaScript?
gotchas.answer: A `Map` remembers insertion order. On `get`, delete and re-insert the key to mark it most recent. On `set`, if the size exceeds the limit, delete `map.keys().next().value`, the oldest key.
